dedupe_keys.name: opennet georgia digital map of the national fibre optic backbone

description: The OpenNet digital map shows the fibre-optic backbone of Georgia, including network nodes (points of presence) and their interconnections. Contents: an interactive map built following the Open Fiber Data Standard (OFDS), information on service availability and technical specifications, a catalogue of wholesale services (dark fibre and data transmission), base layers from ArcGIS and settlement names from Geostat, and an order function for services between two points of presence. The map page states the data were last updated on 4 September 2026. Producer: OpenNet, the state-funded national backbone operator, which aims to give private operators access to affordable capacity so they can build retail networks. Coverage: Georgia. Access: the map can be downloaded as KML and XLS files from the page, with no login needed for the map; the ordering function is restricted to undertakings authorised by the national regulator COMCOM. Licence and cost: free to view and download; no licence text was read on the page. Caveats: the data show the operator's own network only, and route geometry accuracy and the extent of the download were not verified. Simulation uses: the node and route layers provide topology for resilience and hazard-exposure analyses of a national backbone and for Caucasus regional connectivity studies. Related record: the good-practice fibre wiki (data-open-telecom-data-good-practice-fibre-maps) that first highlights this map.
